title: I let Opus choose what to build. It made a game where the weapons are musical instruments.
author: cosmintrica
selftext:
I had $191 in credits that were about to expire, and I was curious what Opus could do if I didn't give it an idea. I asked it to build something worth the money. :))))

It picked a game, PULSEBOUND. You move around dodging enemies, and your weapons are musical instruments. The kick drum sends out shockwaves, the arpeggiator fires lasers. When you pick a new instrument, you hear it join the music too. You can keep the track from a run and export it as a WAV.

It chose the idea, mechanics and original design. After that I kept playing it, asking for changes and polishing it. The first boss felt almost impossible, level-up screens interrupted the drop, and the tutorial needed to show players what to do. The game also uses AI-generated artwork.

The $191 was the starting budget, enough for the first basic version. I then used another $1,700 from the Claude Startup Program, which was also about to expire, plus my subscription allowance. More changes, testing and eventually mobile apps followed.

Technically it's vanilla JavaScript, a custom WebGL2 renderer and a procedural composer that synthesizes the music live through Web Audio. It grew to include cloud saves and leaderboards too.

One thing the first players caught: there were too many tutorial interruptions. I'd been switching tips off during my own runs, so I hadn't noticed how often they interrupted a new player.

It's out on iOS, Android and the web, free to play: [https://playpulsebound.com/app](https://playpulsebound.com/app)

Has anyone else tried letting the agent choose the whole project? Curious what it picked.
